name: Sonnet+tools small/mid-cap growth
strategy: Long-only basket of small/mid-cap cloud, AI-infra, and fintech growth names sized by current momentum and stress-window resilience, with a cash buffer

positions.thesis: Samsara at $40.88 (+6.96% Aug7), Strong Buy consensus, $44.31 avg PT; AI-ops/agentic momentum and $2B ARR story intact, hold at prior sizing as the highest-conviction leader.
Rubrik at $90.07 (+6.47% Aug7), Strong Buy, new Loop Capital $100 PT and Rubrik Agent Identity launch; still ~6% consensus upside into an Aug 27 print, hold at prior sizing.
Affirm at $75.25 with a fresh wave of aggressive PT hikes (BofA $93, Goldman $106, Citi $115) pushing consensus upside to ~21%; upsized off the improving analyst picture into the Aug 27 print.
Flywire beat Q2 revenue ($167.74M vs $156.02M cons) with PT raises to $22-24, but Truist cut to Hold on 2026 growth-deceleration risk; held flat pending resolution of that concern.

Toast beat Q2 (rev $1.91B vs $1.87B cons, EPS $0.26 vs $0.13 YoY), raised FY EBITDA guide to $805-825M, and drew upgrades to $42-45 PTs - the catalyst the prior 'no near-term catalyst' thesis was waiting on has now arrived; upsized off placeholder size.

SentinelOne rallied to $21.40, now trading ABOVE the $19.68 analyst-consensus target near its 52-week high; the 'cheap after a 63% slump' edge that justified 8% is gone, cut to a residual watch position ahead of the Aug 27 print.

UiPath spiked +7.5% to $15.05 on pre-earnings positioning, extending further past the $13.25 Hold-consensus target (-12% implied); the 'no edge' call is more true than a week ago, trimmed further to a token stake.

SoFi's post-earnings analyst cuts (Goldman to $18, Morgan Stanley to $15) confirm growth-spending concerns are weighing on the multiple despite a Q2 beat; held at the already-reduced size with a tight stop.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-08: Prices through 8/7 close (one week after the 7/31 build) confirm momentum is strengthening in the top sleeve (IOT +6.96% Aug7 to $40.88 on continued Buy coverage; RBRK +6.47% to $90.07 with a new Loop Capital $100 PT initiation and an AI-agent-identity product launch; AFRM getting materially more bullish targets - BofA $93, Goldman $106, Citi $115 - vs. the ~$83 that justified the original 18% weight) while two names have lost the edge that justified their sizing: S rallied to $21.40, now trading ABOVE the $19.68 analyst-consensus target near its 52-week high - the 'cheap after a 63% slump' thesis is gone, it's priced for perfection into an Aug 27 print with no analyst upside left; PATH spiked +7.50% to $15.05 on pre-earnings positioning, extending well past the already-unfavorable $13.25 Hold-consensus target (now -12% implied), so the 'no edge, residual size' call is more true than a week ago, not less. TOST delivered the exact catalyst its thesis was waiting on: Q2 beat (rev $1.91B vs $1.87B cons, EPS $0.26 vs $0.13 YoY), raised full-year EBITDA guide to $805-825M, and upgrades to $42-45 PTs (Bernstein, JPMorgan) - the prior 'consensus Hold, no catalyst' framing is stale, so it's upsized off a placeholder-sized position. FLYW beat Q2 revenue ($167.74M vs $156.02M) with several PT raises but also a Truist downgrade on deceleration risk, so it's held flat pending Truist's concern playing out. SOFI's post-earnings analyst cuts (Goldman to $18, Morgan Stanley to $15) confirm the prior 'stress-window resilience broke' call was correct - kept at its already-cut size. Net effect: trims fund adds, gross stays at 95% / cash 5%, this is a rebalance driven by fresh, dated catalysts (TOST/FLYW Aug 4 earnings, this week's analyst target moves), not churn.
